questions.text: Describe a family member you spend a lot of time with.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a family member you spend a lot of time with. You should say: who this person is; what you usually do together; how often you see each other; and explain why you spend so much time with this person.

questions.text: Did you spend as much time with this person when you were younger?
questions.say: Thank you. Did you spend as much time with this person when you were younger?

questions.text: What kinds of things do families in your country like to do together?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a family member you spend a lot of time with, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all family life. What kinds of things do families in your country like to do together?

questions.text: Why do some families spend less time together than in the past?
questions.say: Why do some families spend less time together than in the past?

questions.text: Is it important for families to eat together? Why?
questions.say: Is it important for families to eat together? Why?

questions.text: How have families in your country changed over the last fifty years?
questions.say: Now let's talk about families today. How have families in your country changed over the last fifty years?
